title: Set Theory and Venn Diagrams
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Set Theory and Venn Diagrams. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

coverage: Applications to survey and classification data

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Set language

A set is a collection of distinct elements. (x in A) means x belongs to A; (A subset B) means every element of A is also in B. The universal set contains all elements under discussion. The complement (\(A^c\)) consists of universal elements not in A.

Operations

Union (A union B) includes elements in either set; intersection (A intersect B) includes elements in both. For finite sets, (\(n(A \cup B)=n(A)+n(B)-n(A \cap B)\)); subtract the overlap once because it was counted twice.

Three sets

For three sets, add the individual sizes, subtract each pairwise intersection, then add the triple intersection once. A Venn diagram helps separate 'only A', pair-only regions, the centre overlap, and neither.

Worked example: In a group of 40, 24 study A, 18 study B, and 7 study both. At least one is (\(24+18-7=35\)), so neither is (\(40-35=5\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Fill the centre overlap first when solving a Venn diagram from totals.
  • Distinguish 'A or B' inclusive union from exclusive-or wording.
  • Use the total universe to find the 'neither' region.
  • For three sets, add the triple intersection back after subtracting pairwise overlaps.
  • Check that every disjoint region sums to the stated total.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• (\(n(A \cup B)=n(A)+n(B)-n(A \cap B)\)).
  • (\(n(A^c)=n(U)-n(A)\)).
  • If (A subset B), then (\(A \cap B=A\)) and (\(A \cup B=B\)).
  • For disjoint sets, intersection size is zero.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    In a group of 40, 24 study tea, 18 study coffee, and 10 study both. How many study neither?

    1. (\(6\))
    2. (\(8\))
    3. (\(10\))
    4. (\(12\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(8\))

    Union (\(=24+18-10=32\)). Neither (\(=40-32=8\)).

  2. Core:

    If (\(n(A)=20,n(B)=15,n(A\cap B)=5\)), find (\(n(A\cup B)\)).

    1. (\(25\))
    2. (\(30\))
    3. (\(35\))
    4. (\(40\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(30\))

    Use inclusion-exclusion: (\(20+15-5=30\)).

  3. Foundation:

    If (\(n(A)=20\)), (\(n(B)=15\)), and (\(n(A \cap B)=5\)), find (n(A union B)).

    1. (\(25\))
    2. (\(30\))
    3. (\(35\))
    4. (\(40\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(30\))

    Use inclusion-exclusion: (\(20+15-5=30\)).

  4. Standard:

    In a class of 50, 28 study Hindi, 22 study English and 10 study both. How many study neither?

    1. (\(8\))
    2. (\(10\))
    3. (\(12\))
    4. (\(18\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(10\))

    At least one is (\(28+22-10=40\)). Neither is (\(50-40=10\)).

  5. Challenge:

    In a group of 30, (\(n(A)=16\)), (\(n(B)=14\)), (\(n(A \cap B)=6\)). How many are in A only?

    1. (\(6\))
    2. (\(8\))
    3. (\(10\))
    4. (\(16\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(10\))

    A only is (\(n(A)-n(A \cap B)=16-6=10\)).
